subskill: probability that at least two of three independent events with different probabilities occur
prompt: A production line has three machines, A, B, and C, that operate independently. On any given day, the probabilities that A, B, and C are working are 0.9, 0.8, and 0.7, respectively. The line can run on a day when at least two of the three machines are working. To the nearest thousandth, what is the probability that the line can run on a given day?
explanation: Add the probabilities of the disjoint ways at least two machines work. All three: (0.9)(0.8)(0.7) = 0.504. Exactly two: only C down, (0.9)(0.8)(0.3) = 0.216; only B down, (0.9)(0.2)(0.7) = 0.126; only A down, (0.1)(0.8)(0.7) = 0.056. The total is 0.504 + 0.216 + 0.126 + 0.056 = 0.902. The option "0.846" leaves out the case in which A is the machine that is down. The option "0.896" replaces the three probabilities by their average, 0.8, and uses 3(0.8)²(0.2) + (0.8)³. The option "0.637" averages the three pairwise products, (0.72 + 0.63 + 0.56)/3.
